tools.name: SuggestSkills
tools.description:
Render a card of standalone skills the user can add — org, shared, or Anthropic skills not yet enabled.

Call this when the task is one a skill could make repeatable — drafting in a house style, reviews against a playbook, a recurring workflow — and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about skills. Also when they ask for recommendations, or when ListSkills returned zero matches. Use ListSkills for skills they already have.

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a skill would help, or if you already rendered a suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

Pass keywords drawn from the task itself, and set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). If the result is empty and the trigger was proactive, continue the task without mentioning that you searched; if the user asked, tell them you found nothing new to add.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__add_repo
tools.description:
Add a GitHub repository to the current session so you can read, clone, or operate on it alongside the repos already in the session. Call this whenever you need a repository the session does not have — including when someone only asks a question about one, rather than asking for it to be attached. Prefer attaching a repository over reporting that you cannot reach it. 

IMPORTANT — DO NOT PRE-CHECK THE REPO BEFORE CALLING THIS TOOL. Do not curl github.com, do not run `gh repo view`, do not run `git ls-remote` to verify the repo exists. Unauthenticated requests to private repos return 404 ("Not Found") even when the repo is real and your session has authorized access to it. Those preemptive 404s will mislead you into skipping the tool. Instead: call add_repo with the owner/repo exactly as you have it. The backend performs the real reachability + authorization check and returns a structured error you can act on. If the repo genuinely doesn't exist or isn't accessible, the tool response will tell you — report that to the user. If it does exist, the tool response will include a clone command you can then run. Do not report success until the tool has actually been called and returned. 

WHEN ACCESS IS DENIED: if the tool returns an authorization or policy error — the repo exists but isn't enabled for this workspace/project/organization, or the GitHub App isn't installed or linked — relay the tool's exact reason to the user. The response names the remedy: if Claude doesn't have GitHub access for this organization at all, the user should reconnect GitHub under claude.ai Settings → Connectors; if the repo is simply not in the allowed set, a Claude.ai organization owner can grant access in the settings page the response points to. Do not add settings URLs beyond those provided here or in the tool response. Do not retry the same repo. You may remind the user which repositories are already available in this session, and offer to help them request access. Do not guess, infer, or list repositories you cannot see in the tool res… [truncated]

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__add_repo

Add a GitHub repository to the current session so you can read, clone, or operate on it alongside the repos already in the session. Call this whenever you need a repository the session does not have — including when someone only asks a question about one, rather than asking for it to be attached. Prefer attaching a repository over reporting that you cannot reach it. 

IMPORTANT — DO NOT PRE-CHECK THE REPO BEFORE CALLING THIS TOOL. Do not curl github.com, do not run `gh repo view`, do not run `git ls-remote` to verify the repo exists. Unauthenticated requests to private repos return 404 ("Not Found") even when the repo is real and your session has authorized access to it. Those preemptive 404s will mislead you into skipping the tool. Instead: call add_repo with the owner/repo exactly as you have it. The backend performs the real reachability + authorization check and returns a structured error you can act on. If the repo genuinely doesn't exist or isn't accessible, the tool response will tell you — report that to the user. If it does exist, the tool response will include a clone command you can then run. Do not add settings URLs beyond those provided here or in the tool response. Do not retry the same repo. You may remind the user which repositories are already available in this session, and offer to help them request access. access.description: What access this session needs. "read" (default): fetch/clone only — when the repository is public, git read access is often already served by the session's git proxy with nothing to attach, and the tool says so instead of attaching. "push": the session must push commits, open PRs, or use GitHub API tools against the repository, so it is attached with credentials after the full repository-access checks.

owner.description: GitHub owner (user or organization) of the repo to add, e.g. "anthropics".

repo.description: GitHub repo name, e.g. "claude-code". Do not include the owner prefix — pass owner and repo as separate fields.

tools.description: Archive a Claude Code Remote session. Transitions the session to read-only archived state and releases its container. Use this when a child session has finished its work or is stuck (PR merged, task complete, session failed to initialize) and a human has already acknowledged they're done with the session.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__create_session
tools.description: Create a new Claude Code Remote session. Returns the new session's ID and status. If environment_id is omitted, the new session inherits the calling session's environment. Combine with send_message for fan-out orchestration: spawn a sibling and send it a task. Where enabled, this session receives a <child-session-event> turn if the new session's turn fails or its worker restarts and drops background tasks; a session that finishes cleanly does not report back, so check on it with get_session (status_bucket reads 'failed' for a turn that errored, where status alone reads 'idle' either way) and list_events.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__create_session
schema.description: Create a new Claude Code Remote session. Returns the new session's ID and status. If environment_id is omitted, the new session inherits the calling session's environment. Combine with send_message for fan-out orchestration: spawn a sibling and send it a task. Where enabled, this session receives a <child-session-event> turn if the new session's turn fails or its worker restarts and drops background tasks; a session that finishes cleanly does not report back, so check on it with get_session (status_bucket reads 'failed' for a turn that errored, where status alone reads 'idle' either way) and list_events.

append_system_prompt.description: Text appended to the new session's system prompt.

blob_limit_kb.description: Optional. Files larger than this many KB are left out of the checkout; git fetches one on demand when a command reads it. Requires source_url. Set it for very large repositories, whose sessions otherwise fail to start for lack of disk space. Ignored when sparse_checkout_paths is set.

clone_depth.description: Optional number of commits of history to fetch (default 50). Requires source_url. Lower it for very large repositories.

environment_id.description: Environment ID — a tagged ID starting with 'env_' (or 'ccpool_' for self-hosted pools). Defaults to the calling session's environment. Do NOT invent a value — call list_environments to get the user's real environment_ids. When this resolves to the remote_cowork environment (explicitly or via inheritance), a Claude Cowork session is spawned — the account's enabled skills, plugins and the Cowork system prompt are assembled server-side, and only prompt, title, model and tags are read (source_url, extra_allowed_tools, append_system_prompt and environment_variables are ignored so the caller cannot widen the tool surface).

extra_allowed_tools.description: Extra tool names pre-approved without a user permission prompt. Entries the calling session does not itself have pre-approved are dropped — the child never carries a grant its parent lacks.

model.description: Model ID for the new session. Defaults to the calling session's model.

outcome_branch.description: Optional branch name to push changes to. When set, the session pushes directly to this branch (no session-derived suffix appended).

permission_mode.description: Initial permission mode for the new session. Cannot be more permissive than the calling session's mode; omit to inherit it. 'plan' makes the agent propose a plan and then BLOCKS waiting for human approval via the claude.ai/code web UI — do NOT use 'plan' for autonomous child sessions that no human is watching, as they will stall indefinitely at the approval prompt.

prompt.description: Optional initial message to send to the new session.

source_revision.description: Optional git branch, tag, or commit to check out. Requires source_url. Defaults to the repo's default branch.

source_url.description: Optional git repository URL to check out.

sparse_checkout_paths.description: Optional directories, relative to the repository root. The checkout holds only these, plus the files directly in their parent folders and at the root. Requires source_url. Set it to work in part of a very large repository.

tags.description: Free-form tags to categorize the session (e.g. ["remote-agents-project:frontend"]). Editable later via set_session_tags.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__create_trigger
tools.description: Create a Routine (scheduled trigger). Three targeting modes: (1) default — fires into THIS SESSION, resuming the same conversation each time; (2) persistent_session_id set — fires into a SPECIFIC OTHER SESSION you name (must be in your account); (3) create_new_session_on_fire=true — spawns a FRESH SESSION in this environment on each firing. Use mode 1 for recurring work you want to pick back up yourself; mode 2 for waking a sibling session you created; mode 3 when each firing should start from a clean slate. If the result warns that the Routine stores no connectors, say so plainly when you confirm the Routine to the user and pass on the remedy it names; never report such a Routine as simply created.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__create_trigger
schema.description: Create a Routine (scheduled trigger). Three targeting modes: (1) default — fires into THIS SESSION, resuming the same conversation each time; (2) persistent_session_id set — fires into a SPECIFIC OTHER SESSION you name (must be in your account); (3) create_new_session_on_fire=true — spawns a FRESH SESSION in this environment on each firing. Use mode 1 for recurring work you want to pick back up yourself; mode 2 for waking a sibling session you created; mode 3 when each firing should start from a clean slate. If the result warns that the Routine stores no connectors, say so plainly when you confirm the Routine to the user and pass on the remedy it names; never report such a Routine as simply created.

connectors.description: Optional list of connector names the Routine's fired sessions may use, e.g. ["Gmail", "linear"]. Pass ONLY connectors the user explicitly asked this Routine to use — the stored grant applies to every future firing. Names resolve against the user's connected claude.ai connectors; when calling from inside a CCR session the list is further limited to connectors that session itself holds (it can only narrow that set, never widen it). Any name that cannot be resolved fails the call. Pass [] to store no connectors. Omit to keep the default behavior for this surface. The grant attaches the connectors only — individual tool calls from fired sessions still go through runtime permission checks.

create_new_session_on_fire.description: If true, each firing creates a fresh session in the calling session's environment instead of resuming an existing one. Default false. Mutually exclusive with persistent_session_id.

cron_expression.description: Standard 5-field cron expression (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week), evaluated in UTC. Convert local times to UTC first, using the offset currently in effect. If the conversion crosses midnight, shift the day fields that are set, day-of-week and/or day-of-month (e.g. weekdays at 5pm in UTC-07:00 is 0 0 * * 2-6). Minimum interval is normally hourly (some projects allow shorter); a too-frequent schedule is rejected and the error names the minimum. For hourly or every-N-hours schedules, use minute 0 (e.g. '0 * * * *', '0 */4 * * *'): the server anchors it to the creation minute ('hourly starting now'), so Routines spread across the hour instead of all firing at :00. All other schedules are stored verbatim. Mutually exclusive with run_once_at. Omit both for a poke-only Routine that never fires on its own schedule.

environment_id.description: Environment ID — a tagged ID starting with 'env_' (or 'ccpool_' for self-hosted pools). Defaults to the calling session's environment. Required when calling from outside a CCR session (no session context to inherit from). Do NOT invent a value — call list_environments to get the user's real environment_ids.

initiation.description: Who wanted this: human_request — a person asked you to set this up now; human_schedule — a schedule a person set (e.g. an earlier firing) told you to; own_followup — your own check-in or follow-up on work you are already doing; own_initiative — you decided on your own that this should exist.

notifications.description: Completion notifications for this Routine. push sends to the owner's phone when a run finishes with something noteworthy; email sends the same summary to their inbox. If omitted, the setting stays unset and the server default applies at fire time. Passing this sets an explicit per-Routine choice, so list every channel you want on ({push:true, email:true} for both; {email:true} alone means email-only, push off). Pass {} to opt out of all channels. Only fresh-session-per-fire Routines (create_new_session_on_fire=true) take this; the server rejects it for self-bind or persistent_session_id Routines.

persistent_session_id.description: Optional session ID to fire into instead of this one. Must belong to the same account — the server rejects sessions you don't own. Omit to fire into this session (default). Mutually exclusive with create_new_session_on_fire.

prompt.description: The message the Routine sends on each firing. When binding to an existing session (modes 1-2), write it assuming past context — the conversation continues. In fresh-session mode (mode 3), write it as a complete standalone instruction since each firing starts from nothing.

run_once_at.description: RFC3339 timestamp for a one-shot fire (e.g. 2026-04-20T17:00:00Z). Must be in the future. Mutually exclusive with cron_expression — set one or the other, not both. After the one-shot fires the Routine disables itself with ended_reason=run_once_fired.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__delete_trigger
tools.description: Delete a Routine (scheduled trigger). The Routine must belong to the calling session's account — deleting another account's Routine fails with not-found. Use this to undo a create_trigger call or to clean up Routines whose work is done. A bad cron or wrong prompt does not need deletion — update_trigger fixes those in place, keeping the Routine's run history. On success, the result usually echoes the deleted Routine's last state (including its name) in the response's trigger field — callers without stored-data read access get a plain-text confirmation instead. Either way the Routine no longer exists once this returns.

Optionally include a text message that is appended as an extra user turn after the Routine's configured prompt, so you can pass run-specific context (an error message, a PR link, a diff) into that one firing.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__get_session
tools.description: Get details for a specific Claude Code Remote session by ID. Returns the session's title, status, status_bucket (working / blocked / review_ready / completed / failed — 'failed' means its last turn errored), creation time, and context. Every returned session carries three model fields: configured_model is the model stored at creation, echoed as stored (it may be an alias or carry a context-window suffix, so normalize before comparing); session_context.model is the model the session is currently set to run (the creation-time model, or a later switch or refusal fallback); external_metadata.last_served_model is the model the CLI ran the latest turn on, which also reflects turn-scoped fallbacks (overload or unavailable) that do not change session_context.model. To detect a switch or fallback in a child session, compare configured_model against both session_context.model and external_metadata.last_served_model; the fallback notices in list_events give the reason. Omit session_id to describe this session.

Cowork sessions are tagged "cowork-local" or "cowork-remote" and are excluded from the default (untagged) listing — pass those tags here to list them. tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__list_triggers
tools.description: List Routines (scheduled triggers) owned by this account. Use it to find trigger IDs (trig_...) for update_trigger and delete_trigger. From a thread in a Slack channel, only Routines that fire into that thread's session are listed unless all_in_channel is true. Each entry has the Routine's id, name, cron_expression, run_once_at, enabled state, ended_reason, next_run_at, created_at, persistent_session_id, and last_run. last_run is the most recent recorded run {status, fired_at, finished_at, session_id}. It is absent when no run was recorded (e.g. never fired). For a Routine that wakes an existing session, last_run records that the wake was delivered (SUCCEEDED) or failed to deliver, not how the turn went, unless run tracking covers that session. A FAILED or repeatedly non-SUCCEEDED last_run means the Routine is not doing its job. ended_reason says why a disabled Routine is permanently disabled. suspension_reason (e.g. subscription_paused) marks a temporary hold that lifts when the owner's subscription resumes. Both empty means user-paused. One-shot Routines that already fired (e.g. delivered send_later reminders) and Routines moved to a project are hidden unless include_completed is true. Scheduled tasks stored locally by the Cowork desktop app are not listed.

A FAILED or repeatedly non-SUCCEEDED last_run means the Routine is not doing its job. ended_reason says why a disabled Routine is permanently disabled. suspension_reason (e.g. subscription_paused) marks a temporary hold that lifts when the owner's subscription resumes. all_in_channel.description: Threads in a Slack channel only. If true, list every Routine in this channel, including other threads' and ones that start a new session each time they fire. Default false.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response's next_cursor. Omit for the first page.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__send_later
tools.description: Schedule a message to be delivered back into THIS SESSION at a future time. The message arrives as an ordinary user turn, so you can use it to remind yourself to resume work, check on something, or continue after a delay. Delivery survives container restarts. Granularity is one minute — the scheduler polls every minute, so sub-minute precision is not available. This is a thin wrapper over create_trigger (a self-bind + run_once_at Routine); the returned trigger_id can be passed to delete_trigger to cancel before it fires, and the Routine disables itself after firing once.

Granularity is one minute — the scheduler polls every minute, so sub-minute precision is not available. name.description: Short human-readable label for this reminder as it appears in the user's Routines list (e.g. "Re-check PR #123 CI"). A few words, one line. Optional — omit and one is derived from the message.

To take over, the steward must be opted out first (remove its watching label on the PR).

content.content:
---
name: backfilling-provenance
description: Filling a pack's empty provenance files from its history. Use when a pack under packs/ or .claudinite/local/packs/ carries empty provenance files, or when asked to backfill or write a pack's provenance.
metadata:
  body: workflow
  usage:
    expect: judgment
---

# Backfilling a pack's provenance

The marking pass gave every carrier an empty file; this is how the history goes in. It is a
one-off done by hand because the judgment is what the pass is for: which sentence of a README
is history, which commit was the decision, which field the evidence carries and which it does
not. The tool gathers; every call it cannot make honestly it hands over rather than guessing,
so the sections it prints without a draft under them are the run's work, not its leftovers.

## The run, per pack

0. **Load [changing-pack-elements](../changing-pack-elements/SKILL.md) first.** The run edits
   `provenance/`, `README.md` and `pack.mjs`, each of which forces it - but `apply` writes
   through the tool rather than `Edit`, and the pre-edit guard reads only `Edit`/`Write`, so
   nothing holds the run until the Stop hook, with every file already written.
1. **Take one pack** and list what is owed: `node packs/claudinite-growth/provenance.mjs
   check <pack>` prints what each file is named by, which are empty, which hold only the
   conversion's entry and so owe history too, and how many candidates `_declined.md` already
   holds. The listing is the whole pass: nothing owed is left off it (in a member the tool is
   `.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/provenance.mjs`).
2. **Write the brief**, source-first: `provenance.mjs brief <pack> > brief.md` (an element
   list after the pack narrows it to those files) reads every empty file's history out of
   git, pull request first: each commit's body once, then a draft entry per element it bore
   or changed with the fields git vouches for - the date, the kind, the actor, the model,
   the carrier as `Mechanism`, `Landed` with the version - and the commit's shared fields in
   one `entry-defaults` fence ahead of its entries. Read the tracker comments and the issues
   each body names on GitHub; `history <pack> <element>` prints one element's raw evidence
   where the brief's derivation looks wrong. A shallow clone reads as no history: unshallow
   before trusting an empty brief.

   Four things the brief hands over rather than answering, each printed where it arises.
   **The issues a commit references** are listed beside the defaults fence and never written
   into `Landed`: the trailer's keyword is the branch author's and the pull request body's is
   usually a different one, `Closes` being what fills GitHub's Development panel where `Refs`
   links nothing there - so read the body and write that keyword. **An element older than the
   carrier it sits in** gets its own section: the birth is drafted at the earlier carrier that
   held its text and the later commit re-read as the move or conversion it is, which is a
   derivation to verify against the old path (`git show <sha>:<old path>`), not to trust.
   **A birth the search could not go behind** gets another: the element's text is nowhere
   earlier, but a listing named it before its carrier did or the birth commit took text out
   of another carrier - so the drafted birth is an assumption, and an element reworded on its
   way across is exactly what no text search can follow. Read the evidence named beside each.
   **A pack that has moved** says so under the header, and its inventory covers every path it
   has lived at, so rows naming a file in full are from before the move.
3. **Work the commit inventory before the drafts.** The drafts cover what a carrier's own
   text shows changing, which is less than the pack's history; the brief's *every commit that
   touched this pack* table is the rest, each row carrying the files it touched, the version
   row that claims it, and what it drafts. Two kinds of row are where the decisions hide. A
   row reading **NOTHING DRAFTED** changed something no carrier's text shows - a manifest
   field, a rule's rationale moving out to the README - so read its files before passing it.
   A row marked **sweep** is kept out of the drafts because a sweep usually re-wraps what it
   touches, but where its diff shows it *deciding* something about one element, that element
   owes the entry: touching twelve packs is not deciding nothing here. Read the version rows
   with them, the claimed ones and the *version rows no commit here claims* section alike -
   a row is the maintainer's own words for the decision a version was cut for, and often the
   only place a move is described as a decision at all.
4. **Derive the entries from that evidence before re-reading the rule**, then diff against
   what the rule implied. The first entry is `born` - where the lesson came from, why it
   says what it says, who decided, the carrier and its trigger and why (`Mechanism`), what
   lost (`Rejected`), what would retire it, and `Landed` as the pull request and pack
   version. Then one entry per decision the history shows: a rewording, a split, a move
   into a skill, a conversion to a check, a severity change, a policy change. A file the
   conversion filled from `references.md` is written the same way, its converted entry read as
   evidence: the `Reason` and `Retire when` move by hand onto the entries they actually
   evidence. The placeholder `born` itself is the tool's to resolve - `apply --backfill`
   drops it where the derived birth is earlier and keeps it where its date *is* the birth -
   so read each such file's own evidence rather than truncating them as a class.
5. **Write only what the evidence carries.** A field with nothing behind it is omitted,
   never filled with a placeholder or a plausible guess: a fabricated rationale lets a
   future review reaffirm a rule on false grounds, which is worse than no rationale. An
   element whose history the evidence does not reach gets a `born` entry that says only
   what is known - the date and commit it first appears in - and stays as short as that.
   Where the pack's evidence names a member per rule rather than rule by rule, the shared
   `Source` goes on the defaults fence and the per-element one is left off: an attribution
   split finer than the evidence is a guess wearing a citation.
6. **Write the entries in hyphens**, not long dashes - `no-new-long-dashes` fires on
   every file that carries one, and a backfill writing a pack's history in one pass earns
   the finding twenty-nine times over and a second commit to undo it.
7. **Edit the brief, then apply it**: `Source`, `Reason`, `Rejected` and `Retire when` go on
   the commit's defaults fence where every element it bore shares them, and on one entry
   where they are its own; a draft the commit did not decide is deleted, and the kind a
   draft guessed (`reworded` for any later commit) is corrected to what the change was.
   `provenance.mjs apply <pack> brief.md --backfill` validates every entry as one batch,
   writes each file in date order under its defaults, and writes nothing while any one is
   refused; run twice it writes nothing new. **`--backfill` is what this run is entitled to
   and no other caller is**: a backfill derives history that already happened, so its entries
   are dated before whatever the file holds, which the ordinary append lane refuses and
   should. It is also what lets a run open the file for an element retired before the marking
   pass, where the batch runs from `born` through `retired` - such a history never goes on
   `_pack.md`, which a `retired` entry would seal. An entry the brief cannot carry - a split
   across files, a declined candidate - goes through `append <pack> <element>`, the entry on
   stdin. A mechanism the
   pack shares across elements - why a skill loads on these paths, why the release set
   vendors as stubs - is written once, on the element that owns it, and cited from the
   others.
8. **Trim the README and the manifest's header comment in the same change.** Each sentence
   of history the README holds (the "distilled from" paragraph, the "until #n", the "kept
   as it was", a mechanism's reasons) is evidence this run has already read, so it moves
   onto the entry it evidences and leaves the README, which keeps only what a person
   adopting the pack does with it. Work the brief's *README sections* list rather than its
   sentence tells: the tells find history that dates or numbers itself, while a section
   explaining why an element reads as it does carries neither and is the half most often
   left behind. The list counts each section's tables separately, and a table is weighed
   like any other prose rather than skipped: a table of evidence or of per-member findings
   is history and moves onto the entries it evidences, while a catalog of what the pack
   carries stays. In one pack the single largest piece of history was a table. The header comment of `pack.mjs` is the pack-level
   record `_pack.md` is written from - why the pack exists, why it fingerprints as it does
   or not at all, what it carries and why - so its decisions become `_pack` entries and the
   header keeps what a reader of the code needs: what the pack is, in a few lines. Report
   both files' bytes before and after in the pull request body.
9. **Candidates the history shows were turned down** - an extraction the owner declined, a
   conversion judged not checkable - go on `_declined.md`, kind `declined`, with `Source`,
   `Reason` and `Actor`, so the next pass reads them before nominating.
10. **Finish with `provenance.mjs check <pack>` reporting no fault** - it prints its
    file-to-carrier listing either way, so the pass is that listing alone and exit 0, never
    silence - the repo's offline suite green, and a pull request carrying the pack's
    provenance files, its trimmed README, its trimmed manifest and nothing else, titled `Provenance: backfill <pack>` and referencing
    the tracking issue. One pack per pull request is the default, and a pack whose elements
    arrived across several pull requests stays one; what a run costs is the reading, so
    packs whose history is one pull request apiece batch into one. Predict the automerge
    policy as each pack's `provenance/`, `README.md` and `pack.mjs` - the manifest trim is
    part of the method - and name the packs rather than reaching for a `packs/**` wildcard,
    which stops the policy being a prediction of the diff.

## What never happens here

- No carrier changes. A rule that reads wrong is a later change with its own entry; the
  backfill records what was decided, not what should have been.
- No entry restates the rule. The carrier is the description; the entry is the decision.
- No `Actor` is an email, no session id or quoted exchange lands in a canon file, and no
  field is written to look complete.

# The method

Follow `packs/claudinite-growth/skills/backfilling-provenance/SKILL.md` exactly, all 10 steps. Read it in full before doing anything. Load the `changing-pack-elements` skill first, as its step 0 says. - Never edit anything under `.claudinite/shared/` — it is vendored and replaced wholesale.

`provenance.mjs brief claudinite-growth` is ~452 KB. The pack has MOVED repeatedly: its history reads under `packs/claudinite-growth`, `packs/grow_with_claudinite`, `.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation`, `.claudinite/local_packs/canon-curation`, `skills/prose-to-checks`, `skills/unattended-agents`, `packs/core` and `packs/basics`. The brief says so under its header. Rows naming a file in full are from before the move. Expect many inventory rows whose files are all under `packs/basics/` — that is the era before the content moved out, and some of those rows really did decide something about an element that now lives here.

# Four findings from the two backfills already merged (#2263, #2265) — apply them

1. **The load-bearing one: the brief cannot follow a rule reworded on its way across a compaction pass.** When a sweep rewrites a corpus, the text search loses the trail and the brief drafts a `born` AT THE COMPACTION rather than at the run that actually landed the rule — and it does NOT flag these under "births the search could not go behind". In the home's local pack this was 69 drafted births across two compaction PRs; 48 belonged at the real earlier runs and only 17 legitimately stayed (clauses split into rules of their own). So: for every drafted `born` whose commit is a sweep, a compaction, a "tighten every RULES.md" or a corpus rewrite, go behind it by hand — `provenance.mjs history <pack> <element>`, `git log -S` on a distinctive phrase, `git show <sha>:<old path>` across the pack's old paths — before accepting the date. 2. **Reference keywords disagree between the commit trailer and the PR body in roughly a third of PRs.** In one case the trailer named a different ISSUE from the body (trailer `Refs #592`, body `Closes #593`). `Landed` must carry the keyword from the real GitHub PR body, read via the GitHub MCP tools (`mcp__github__pull_request_read`), never the trailer. Batch these reads.
3. **A drafted `reworded` is often really `scope-changed` or `severity-changed`.** Read what the diff did: a check whose path anchor changed scope, or whose severity moved, is not a rewording. Correct the kind.
4. **The `--backfill` lane is the only one entitled to write past-dated entries**, and `apply` writes the whole brief as one validated batch. `append` takes exactly ONE entry per invocation on stdin — it rejects multi-entry stdin with `expected exactly one entry, found N`. One call per entry.

Base directory for this skill: /home/user/Claudinite/.claude/skills/searching-for-a-tool

# Searching for a tool

- **A search that finds nothing** is evidence about your query, not about the environment: vary
  the query before concluding a capability is absent, and try the tool before telling the owner a
  step is theirs. (search-finds-nothing)
- **`select:` takes a short name as readily as a qualified one** — `select:get_teams` and
  `select:mcp__github__get_teams` both return the tool, and a comma-separated list loads several at
  once. Qualify a name two servers could both carry. (select-takes-short)
- **A bare short name is a keyword query, and resolves too** — `get_teams` on its own returns the
  tool, ranked above the looser matches beneath it. (bare-short-name)
- **A server whose whole roster the deferred-tools listing already names** is the one exception: one
  miss there is the answer, so read the roster rather than rephrase the query. (server-whole-roster)

- **`textAndFileManipulation.md`** — the three bullets on searching/rewriting text across files (grep for inbound references before delete/rename; naive repo-wide string-replace corruptions; grep/sed rename passes missing `path.join` segments).

Both follow the existing corpus shape (H1 + portable-scope framing + cross-references) and are registered in the README and the routine's routing table. `engineeringPractices.md` keeps the genuinely-general remainder and points at both new siblings.

- New **§4c "Accept → create a new corpus doc (rare)"** with a high bar and a bounded write surface (new doc + README + routing-table row), human-review backstop, never a direct push/merge.

{"number":66,"title":"Loosen the bar for creating a new corpus file/cluster","body":"## What

Makes a **new** corpus file/cluster learnable. A new file is now admissible whenever the candidate lesson clears the full Worthiness bar — (a) distilled, (b) portable, (c) durable and reusable, (d) not already covered anywhere in the corpus — **and** no existing file's scope genuinely fits it. Nothing more.

Dropped the extra new-file-only hurdles:
- the "expect it to recur" requirement,
- the "would distort an existing file" requirement,
- the "default to reject when unsure" tiebreak *as applied to the new-file decision*.

Kept intact:
- **Routing into an existing file is the first choice** — a new file is for when none fits, not a way to dodge folding into an existing owner.

{"number":113,"title":"Add tasks/agentic-documentation.md — source-audited rewrite (for #111)","body":"Independent, **from-scratch** version of the "how to write instruction docs for Claude" doc requested in #111 — built by verifying each claim directly against the primary Anthropic sources, without reading the earlier draft (to avoid inheriting its framing). An alternative to #112 for comparison; **do not merge without picking one.**

### What this doc is
A mounted practice doc owning the **craft of writing instruction docs** for Claude — read before authoring a practice doc, a project `CLAUDE.md`, or a routine spec. 36 lines, imperative bullets, self-applying, every non-obvious rule cited inline to a Sources footer.

### Verified against primary text
Each claim was checked against the fetched primary text (not search summaries):
- **Right altitude** — quoted accurately: *"Goldilocks zone between two common failure modes"* and *"specific enough to guide behavior effectively, yet flexible enough to provide the model with strong heuristics"* ([context engineering](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents)).
- **Terseness = adherence** — *"Bloated CLAUDE.md files cause Claude to ignore your actual instructions"* ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices)); *"smallest possible set of high-signal tokens"* (context engineering).
- **~200-line budget** — *"target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file … reduce adherence"* ([memory](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory)). Scoped to **always-loaded files**, not all instruction docs; `@`-imports still load at launch, so they don't save context.
- **Verifiable imperatives** — the doc's exact examples (*"Use 2-space indentation"*, *"Run `npm test` before committing"*) come straight from the memory docs; **no-contradiction** is the memory "Consistency" rule.
- **Examples** — corrected from "used sparingly" to **one of the most reliable steering tools**: a few (3–5) diverse, canonical examples in `<example>` tags, not *"a laundry list of edge cases"* (context engineering + prompt engineering).

### Omissions the sources emphasize, now added
- **Positive over negative** instructions (*tell Claude what to do, not what to avoid*).
- **New-employee / golden rule** (show it to a colleague with no context).
- **Emphasis nuance** — `IMPORTANT`/`YOU MUST` is a real lever, but current models over-trigger on aggressive phrasing; use it sparingly.
- **Instructions vs. hooks** — instructions are advisory; a must-happen-every-time action needs a hook.

### Dedup / single-owner (per #111)
- Relocated the *"rule-plus-constraints / move the why out"* rule **out of `agenticBestPractices.md`** into this doc.
- Registered the doc in the `CLAUDE.md` `tasks/` index.
- Deliberately does **not** restate `growth/item-routing.md` / `extracting-lessons.md` (worthiness/routing/dedup — a separate concern).

{"number":128,"title":"Context-relief architecture: packs (prose + checks) and skills, with enforcement","body":"## What this is

Reorganizes the corpus from always/soft-loaded instructions into **two homes selected by *when* a rule is active**, plus a deterministic enforcement engine:

- **`packs/<name>/`** — a bundle of prose (`RULES.md`) *and* checks, active **once per session** by the project's `.claudinite-checks.json` declaration (`universal` always on). Active packs' prose is injected by a SessionStart hook; their checks run at every Stop and in CI. A dependency-free registry discovers packs by directory scan — no list to maintain.
- **`skills/<name>/`** — activity-scoped procedures the harness surfaces on demand; content inlined in each `SKILL.md` (no cross-tree redirect).
- **`checks/`** — the engine only: the runner, lib, the Stop hook, the PreToolUse guard, and their red-first fixtures.

`always/`, `tasks/`, `technologies/`, and `templates/` are gone — folded into the two homes.

## The model (design in `checks/DESIGN.md`)

- **Promotion ladder**: platform setting → hook → check → skill → prose. A rule lives in the cheapest mechanism that can carry it; prose is the audited fallback.
- **Checks** are declared+closed (every rule of a declared pack runs every time), drift-guarded by a structural fingerprint meta-check; diff-scoped only as a transitional aid (whole-repo sweep is the default); reasoned acceptances; fail-fast severity (advisory is a per-rule *kind*, not a burn-in stage).
- **Platform settings are verified, never trusted** — an offline effect check (squash-only ⇒ no merge commits in main's first-parent history) plus a config check later.
- **Technology gotchas convert per-gotcha** by whether they have a static artifact signature; the rest is pack prose.
- **Skills**: model-invoked routing is probabilistic, so nothing that *must* happen rides on a skill — enforcement is checks/hooks/settings. (Skill-scoped hooks exist, verified, for the rare activity-scoped enforcement need.)
- **Growth is checks-first**: promote descends the ladder for each new lesson; a `prose-to-checks` skill sweeps the existing prose backlog for always-testable rules the conversion missed.

## Implemented (all green: 42 tests, CI passing, sweep clean)

- Runner + registry; **universal pack** (7 checks) + **github-actions** (6) + **chrome-extension** conformance (6); the pack-prose SessionStart loader; the Stop hook and PreToolUse guard.
- Full pack prose (baseline, technology packs, the chrome-extension release standard, the research-project class pack); 12 inlined skills (command + practice) + the prose-to-checks skill.
- Bootstrap Parts 6–7 (hooks, `--init`, skill symlinks); index, README, DESIGN, growth docs all updated to the two-home model.

## The checks earned their keep repeatedly

They caught real defects at every stage — dangling links and a label/href mismatch on `main`; **nine historical merge commits** that had bypassed the squash-only policy unnoticed (now sha-keyed acceptances); real pipefail defects in the canon release workflows; and several of my own regressions mid-restructure (the Stop hook blocked me in-session more than once).

**Owner action outstanding:** flip the squash-only merge *setting* (repo Settings → General) — unreachable from here; the effect check covers the gap meanwhile.

Closes #127
Closes #131

{"number":169,"title":"Fan out fleet maintenance via plain subagents, not the Workflow tool","body":"## Problem

The scheduled **Fleet daily maintenance routine** begins by surfacing a blocking permission dialog — *"Allow Claude to run a workflow fleet-daily-maintenance?"* — before doing any work. An unattended night routine has no human present to click **Allow**, so it stalls on step one.

## Root cause

The routine spec prescribes *"dispatch each per-repo run as its own **subagent**"* with phases and barriers. It never names the Workflow tool — but "phases with barriers, one isolated subagent per repo" maps so cleanly onto the multi-agent-orchestration **`Workflow`** tool that a session implementing the routine reaches for it (the dialog text is a verbatim Workflow `meta` block).

The `Workflow` tool may only be called when the user has **explicitly opted into** multi-agent orchestration, and the harness enforces that with an interactive prompt on **every** run — one that only disappears under bypass-permissions / headless modes a scheduler can't be relied on to be in. So fanning out through the Workflow tool is fundamentally at odds with "runs unattended."

## Fix

Drop the Workflow tool from the routine — fan out with **plain subagent dispatch** (the Agent/Task tool), which has no opt-in gate, exactly as the spec already implied. The orchestrator honors the phase barriers itself.

- `routines/auto-all-repos-maintenance.md` — Step 2, the launcher prompt, and the "never do" list now state explicitly that fan-out uses plain subagent dispatch, never the Workflow orchestration tool, and say why.
- `skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md` — captures the durable, portable rule: an unattended agent must never invoke a tool that surfaces a blocking approval it can't answer; the Workflow tool is the classic trap.

No behavior change to any growth phase — this only pins *how* the orchestrator dispatches.

Closes #168

method.description:
Action to specify what pull request data needs to be retrieved from GitHub. 
Possible options: 
 1. get - Get details of a specific pull request.
 2. get_diff - Get the diff of a pull request.
 3. get_status - Get combined commit status of a head commit in a pull request.
 4. get_files - Get the list of files changed in a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 5. get_commits - Get the list of commits on a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 6. get_review_comments - Get review threads on a pull request. Each thread contains logically grouped review comments made on the same code location during pull request reviews. Returns thread metadata and comments with nullable current and original line-range coordinates (line, start_line, original_line, original_start_line). Current coordinates are omitted when unavailable, such as for outdated comments. Use cursor-based pagination (perPage, after) to control results.
 7. get_reviews - Get the reviews on a pull request. When asked for review comments, use get_review_comments method. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 8. get_comments - Get comments on a pull request. Use this if user doesn't specifically want review comments. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 9. get_check_runs - Get check runs for the head commit of a pull request. Check runs are the individual CI/CD jobs and checks that run on the PR.

{"number":167,"title":"Rework daily-maintenance & release actions: living tracker, fresh failure issues, privacy fold","body":"Closes #166. All changes are canon-only — consumer repos are untouched, so they inherit the new behavior on their next re-bootstrap (stub-shape changes) or next workflow run (reusable-workflow logic, referenced `@main`).

## A — Branch/maintenance report → one living tracker issue
`routines/auto-repo-tidy.md`: the tidy report was a comment-only-when-changed feed. Now there's **one** standing `Repo Tidy Tracker` issue whose **body** is rewritten each run to today's current state (dated, newest snapshot at the top), plus a **dated per-run status comment** as the scrollable trail. The `unattended-agents` skill's standing-tracking-issue guidance gains the general "current-state → keep it in the body, newest at top" pattern.

## B — Action failures → fresh issue per failure + dedup
`.github/actions/report-failure/action.yml`: previously it reopened/appended a single standing per-workflow issue. Now each failure opens a **fresh** `workflow-failure` issue, and any **earlier open** failure issues **for the same workflow** are closed as duplicates of the new one (comment `Duplicate of #N` + close as not planned). The newest failure is always the single open bug to triage; superseded ones collapse behind it. Wording synced in `skills/git-github-advanced`, `packs/github-actions/scheduled-failure-escalation`, and `RELEASE.md`.

Scope note: this deliberately targets the **GitHub Action** that opens bugs for humans. The daily-maintenance orchestrator's own routine self-log (a routine appending dated comments to its own issue) is a different mechanism and is unchanged.

## C — Collapse the privacy-page deploy; keep daily vs manual publish separate
- The standalone `deploy-privacy-page.yml` **stub** is removed and folded into `publish-chrome-store` as a **`privacy_only`** dispatch mode (skips the store upload, only (re)deploys `/privacy/`). This covers the one real standalone use — making the URL live before the first store submission. **4 stubs → 3.** The platform-agnostic `deploy-privacy-page.yml` **reusable workflow** stays in the canon, called from `publish-chrome-store`.
- **Pushback taken on merging daily + manual publish:** I kept `daily-release` and `publish-chrome-store` **separate**. They answer different questions — daily is automatic, shipped-file-gated, patch-bumps, and always ships to users; manual publish targets a chosen/older tag and can upload as a draft (`auto_publish: false`). Merging them into one mode-switched dispatch trades a clean two-verb model for a muddier one exactly when you're doing a delicate manual store publish. Happy to go the other way if you'd prefer the single action.

Contract (`RELEASE.md`), pack README, the `cer/release-workflows` check + its map, and the pack tests are all updated to three stubs.

## Verification
- `node --test checks/test/*.test.mjs` → 75 pass / 0 fail
- `node checks/run.mjs` (conformance over this repo) → exit 0
- All edited YAML re-parses cleanly.

## Assumptions (flip any — say the word)
1. **(B) dedup scope:** same-workflow only. Alternative: close *all* open `workflow-failure` issues as duplicates of the newest regardless of workflow.
2. **(A) comment cadence:** a dated status comment **every** run (per "add a comment about today's status") on top of the body refresh. Alternative: comment only when the picture changed.
3. **(C):** privacy folded, daily + manual publish kept separate (the pushback). Alternative: full merge into one store-release action.

{"number":177,"title":"Routine-authoring guidelines + a skill-owned routine-structure check","body":"## What

Three coupled changes:

1. **`skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md`** — a tightened *"Structuring a routine as prose + scripts"* subsection, led by the folder/naming convention.
2. **Skill-owned checks** — a new discovery mechanism so a skill can carry the test-the-world check that validates its action, co-located with the SKILL.md.
3. **`routine-structure` check** — living in `skills/unattended-agents/`, with its test and manifest beside it.

Closes #178

## The convention + guidelines

A routine is a folder — `dev/routines/<routine-name>/` — with **`routine.md`** as the standard entry point, beside the `preconditions.sh` / `postconditions.sh` it invokes by path. Four rules: bracket the agent's judgment between the two scripts asymmetrically (precondition fail → skip; postcondition fail → terminal, never retry); state in `routine.md` every expectation a check enforces; extract a script only when it consolidates a whole deterministic decision; keep the job in the prose, not in a script's comments.

## Skill-owned checks (the placement fix)

A skill defines an *action*, so the test-the-world check validating that action's result belongs **beside the SKILL.md**, not in the universal pack. This adds that capability:

- `skills/registry.mjs` discovers any `skills/<name>/checks.mjs` (default export = array of rules) structurally, mirroring `packs/registry.mjs`.
- `checks/run.mjs` loads and runs skill rules alongside pack rules, includes them in `--list`; the Stop hook inherits them (it shells out to `run.mjs`). Skill checks are **never declared and always run** (like universal), each inert until its artifact exists.
- CI runs the co-located tests (`skills/*/*.test.mjs`); a runner test proves a skill check is discovered, run, and listed through the CLI.
- Documented in `checks/DESIGN.md`.

`routine-structure` now lives in `skills/unattended-agents/` (check + `routine-structure.test.mjs` + `checks.mjs`), reverting its earlier universal-pack registration.

## The check (`routine-structure`)

Inert until a `routine.md` exists. Assertions:
- **blocking** — a `bash …/x.sh` invocation in `routine.md` resolving to no file;
- **blocking** — a folder with `preconditions.sh`/`postconditions.sh` but no `routine.md` entry point;
- **advisory** — a script the entry point never invokes; a script with no shebang.

Full suite **81/81 green**, conformance sweep clean (the check module's shared `checks/lib` import is accepted the same way the `packs/` acceptance handles it), and the check runs clean against a real routine.

## Provenance

Distilled from a session that iteratively designed a daily fallback-coverage routine, each guideline corresponding to a wrong turn corrected. Deduped against the existing `unattended-agents` bullets; kept project-agnostic.

{"number":225,"title":"Fleet bootstrap sweep: adoption + re-bootstrap + canon alignment, a deterministic coverage census Action, and a per-member PR/push delivery flag","body":"Closes #224.

## What

One routine owns **all bootstrap work across the fleet** — orchestrated entirely from Claude Code's single scheduled fleet routine. After each nightly cycle, every repo under the `missingbulb` account mounts Claudinite with current wiring and current rules, or is explicitly opted out, or sits in the adoption queue awaiting one owner action:

- **`routines/auto-fleet-bootstrap.md`** (85 lines, house register) — the sweep: three steps, one isolated subagent per target repo, API-only.
  - **Step 1 — dispatch the census.** The sweep triggers the **dispatch-only executor**: [`fleet-coverage.yml`](../blob/claude/cloud-knight-daily-routine-t4q24l/.github/workflows/fleet-coverage.yml) (`workflow_dispatch` only — **deliberately no cron**; Claude Code stays the sole orchestrator) running [`check-fleet-coverage.mjs`](../blob/claude/cloud-knight-daily-routine-t4q24l/routines/check-fleet-coverage.mjs) with the **`FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN`** fine-grained PAT (all repositories, Contents+Metadata read, Issues read/write). Contract: classify every repo (covered / uncovered / opted-out / skipped; erroring marker check = unknown-never-uncovered, run fails into the shared `report-failure` escalation; unreadable opt-out list aborts) and converge the **adoption queue** — one `Adopt <owner>/<repo> into the Claudinite fleet` issue (label `fleet-adoption`) per unwired, not-opted-out repo, auto-closed when resolved. All eligibility rules live once, in the script.
  - **Step 2 — members: re-bootstrap + align.** Refresh the mount/wiring per `bootstrap.md` (which owns that list); evaluate against the member's declared packs' current checks and apply a failing check's own remedy — never more; judgment findings become member-repo issues. Enrollment issues: never opened for members, still-open ones closed.
  - **Step 3 — adoption: work the queue.** Adopt only repos with an open adoption issue; unreachable queued repos stay queued (the issue is the owner's cue) and are logged.
- **Delivery flag, always explicit** — every member's `.claudinite-checks.json` carries `"maintenance": { "delivery": "push" | "pr" }`; `--init` seeds `push` (test extended), bootstrap Part 6 backfills existing files, the sweep repairs a missing key as drift; `pr` = never-merged PR on the stable `claudinite/maintenance` branch; unrecognized value = no commits + an issue. The principle extends the avoid-default-values lesson in `skills/engineering-practices/SKILL.md`.
- **`routines/fleet-bootstrap-opt-out.md`** — the owner-maintained opt-out list (gates adoption only; unreadable ≠ empty).
- **Two new canon lessons** in `skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md`: the **dispatch-only executor** pattern (privileged capability wrapped as a triggerable workflow; no cron on executors — one schedule, owned by the orchestrating routine) and **checklist-altitude spec sizing** (contracts not internals, pointers not restatements, re-compress after every scope addition; house norm ~40–90 lines — this spec was 209 before the pass).
- **`routines/auto-all-repos-maintenance.md`** — three sequenced steps, each deferring to its own doc; its launcher sentence slimmed to a thin pointer per its own never-inline rule. **`bootstrap.md`**, **`checks/README.md`**, **`growth/README.md`**, **`README.md`** updated.

## Setup required after merge

Create the **`FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN`** repo secret (fine-grained PAT: this account, all repositories, Contents+Metadata read, Issues read/write). The census has no schedule — it runs when the nightly sweep dispatches it, or manually via *Run workflow*.

## Policy choices worth a look

- Adoption and `push`-mode delivery commit **directly to the target's default branch**; the opt-out list, adoption/enrollment issues, coverage tracker, and the per-member `pr` flag are the control points.
- Forks and archived repos are standing skips, visible in the census summary.

## Verification

- `node --test checks/test/*.test.mjs skills/*/*.test.mjs`: 109 pass, 0 fail (includes the extended `--init` test asserting the seeded flag); `node checks/run.mjs` exits 0.
- Bootstrap Part 6's backfill one-liner exercised against a copy of this repo's real `.claudinite-checks.json`: adds the key once, byte-identical on re-run.
- Census script: `node --check` passes; opt-out parser exercised against the real list, a populated sample, and a heading-less file (throws — unreadable ≠ empty). First live validation: dispatch the workflow after the secret exists.
- **Live permission test** (this session, App on "All repositories"): `search_repositories` enumerated a private never-granted repo prompt-free while `get_file_contents` on it was proxy-denied — the two-gate reality the census PAT and the queue design are built around.

{"number":237,"title":"Structure-review cleanups: co-locate pack tests, catalog drift-guard, doc/helper homes","body":"Cleaner-layout fixes from a structure review of the repo — five changes, all **repo-internal** blast radius (no consumer-referenced path moves). Closes #236, closes #216.

## 1. Co-locate pack tests inside their packs
Each pack now carries one `packs/<pack>/pack.test.mjs` beside the rules it proves; `checks/test/` is left to the engine. The two mixed files are split by owner (`converted.test.mjs`'s engine test → `checks/test/context.test.mjs`; its esbuild tests → aws-sam; `skill-ownership`/`rules` → `packs/basics/pack.test.mjs`). `pack-detect.test.mjs` **stays central** on purpose (it asserts the shared marker-depth convention across several packs, not any one pack) — now header-commented. CI glob + `checks/README` + `prose-to-checks` updated.

**Supersedes the stale PR #221** (which predates the `universal`→`basics` rename and targets the deleted `packs/universal/`); adopts #221's conventions — uniform `pack.test.mjs`, central detect test, and its in-passing `packs/README` fingerprint fix — rebuilt on current `main`. **#221 can be closed.**

## 2. Catalog drift-guard
`packs/README.md`'s table was missing 7 of 17 packs; `CLAUDE.md` listed 11 of 14 skills. Completed the pack table, de-duplicated CLAUDE.md's skill enumeration to a pointer, and added a **`catalog-completeness` check** (basics, corpus-gated) asserting each catalog README lists every collection member on disk — so the index can't silently drift again.

## 3. Home `extracting-lessons.md` with its skill
Moved from `growth/` into `skills/lessons-learned/`, resolving the `skills/README` "no cross-tree redirect" contradiction (a skill's content now lives within its own directory). All 8 referencing files updated.

## 4. Pack-local helper into `lib/`
`chrome-extension-release/manifest-permissions.mjs` → `chrome-extension-release/lib/` so a reader auditing rule modules doesn't mistake the helper for a rule.

## 5. `.github/workflows/README.md`
Classifies each workflow/action as repo CI / fleet orchestration / **frozen `@main` API**, putting the consumer-facing boundary at the point of edit rather than only in `consumer-safe-changes.md`.

## Verification
- `node --test` full suite: **122 pass, 0 fail** under the new globs.
- `node checks/run.mjs` whole-repo conformance sweep: **clean** (confirms no broken links from the moves, and `catalog-completeness` passes on the real tree).

{"number":284,"title":"Dissolve growth/ into packs: canon-curation (home-only) + grow_with_claudinite; drop the growth barriers","body":"Closes #281.

## What this does

**Growth becomes fully pack-based and the top-level `growth/` folder is deleted** (per extending.md: a relocation retires the old home).

### New `canon-curation` pack (home-only)
- `detect: null`, never seeded by `--init` or any migration — declared by hand in exactly one repo: the canon home. **Declaration cardinality enforces "central, once"**: a pack task runs per declaring repo, so one declaring repo means one unit per night, with no bespoke orchestrator step. Gates double-lock with `isHome`.
- Carries **promote** (`growth-promote-to-claudinite`, absorbing `promote.md`, `item-routing.md`, `promote-scope.mjs` + test) and the new weekly **`prose-to-checks-sweep`** task (previously a homeless "periodic central pass").
- Owns the `prose-to-checks` skill (moved off `basics` — it's canon-home activity; members have no canon prose to convert).

### `grow_with_claudinite` absorbs its stage docs
`extract.md`, `dedup.md`, `discover-packs.md` move in next to their `run_daily` descriptors; worker paths updated. Its README now owns the "identifying a project's local docs" method; the lifecycle narrative moved to `canon-curation`'s README.

### No more barriers
Extract, promote, and dedup are ordinary **independent** units (`order: null`); the `growth:N` order tokens, the orchestrator's phased dispatch, and the bespoke post-barrier promote step are all deleted. Each stage reads only what's already **merged**: a lesson extracted tonight is promoted tomorrow night (the extract commit trips the next night's signals) — and promote's PR approval was always the dominant latency. Faster cadences (promote twice daily, or before/after the nightly) stay available without design changes.

### Planner: the home repo is planned too — last
`planAccessibleFleet` captures the home repo instead of skipping it; `buildWorkPlan` plans it after every member, stamping its signal bundle with `isHome: true` and the **`fleetMembers` aggregate** (`{repo, activePacks, projectChanged}` per member). Promote's gate targets exactly the changed members that declare `grow_with_claudinite` (weekly full sweep: all of them) and hands the list to the worker as `targets.repos`. `baselining` self-skips `isHome` (the canon doesn't mount itself).

### Bookkeeping
- Home repo's `.claudinite-checks.json` declares `canon-curation`; the `growth/promote-scope.mjs` file-placement acceptance is retired (covered by the standing `packs/` acceptance at its new home).
- core-independence ACCEPT: all six `growth/*` debt entries pruned; the new pack references in core docs reviewed in; `checks-ci.yml`'s promote write-surface gate accepted under the release-infra reason.
- Stale `DESIGN.md` claim that "the home repo declares no packs" corrected.

## Verification
- `node --test` — 226/226 pass, including new coverage: home-repo planning with the fleet aggregate, promote gate targeting/isolation (changed-vs-enrolled filtering, full-sweep widening, never-off-home), sweep gate, baselining `isHome` skip, and back-compat `buildWorkPlan` without a homeRepo.
- `node checks/run.mjs` — conformance sweep green (validates the new pack declaration and every moved link via reference-integrity).
- No `growth/` path references or `growth:` order tokens remain anywhere.

{"number":294,"title":"Make fleet daily maintenance MCP-native: no REST, census decoupled, migration repo unified","body":"Closes #295.

## Why

The fleet daily-maintenance run went to a **no-op day** (#193): every in-session code step returned **401**. #289 moved the planner + migration passes to run in-session as `node` scripts using a REST `fetch` client + `GITHUB_TOKEN`, but the runtime this routine is *scheduled* in (a Claude Code web session) has **no GitHub REST credential** — only the MCP GitHub tools, which `node` can't call. This PR makes the whole process MCP-native and runnable in its own runtime.

## What changed

**1. No REST in the daily process.** Relocated the REST client `fleet-api.mjs` from `routines/fleet/` to `packs/sheepdog/` — the account-spanning coverage census is its sole legitimate owner (it enumerates `/user/repos`, which MCP can't, and runs as its own Action). Stripped `makeGh` + the `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_REPOSITORY` `main()` wrappers from `plan.mjs`, `fleet-apply.mjs`, `fleet-retire.mjs`.

**2. Writes land as one `push_files` commit; a rare file-move's delete follows via `delete_file` (MCP has no atomic multi-file+delete — and no active migration produces a delete). The apply/retire tests were rewritten to mock the `io` interface; the sequencing stays tested while the orchestrator implements thin MCP primitives.

{"number":325,"title":"unattended-agents: a change-gated routine must exclude its own writes from its triggers","body":"## Lessons-learned capture (post-merge of #322)

The fleet-planner optimization (#322) hit the same trap in two independent forms:

1. The `substantiveChange` filter didn't recognize the baselining worker's subject-initial `Baseline:` commit convention (only `baselining` / `claudinite baseline`), so the nightly mount-refresh commits were scored as real project work and re-fired growth/tidy.
2. Each `repo-tidy` run rewrites its own `Claudinite tracker: Repo Tidy` issue nightly, so that ~24h-old update always sat inside the 25h lookback window — meaning tidy would re-fire on an otherwise-quiet repo *forever*, silently defeating the whole "skip unchanged repos" optimization.

Both are instances of **one portable invariant**: a routine that writes to the repos / issues / artifacts it also monitors must keep its own outputs out of its change-detection inputs. The fleet code and `DESIGN.md` document the specific instances; this promotes the general rule into the `unattended-agents` skill so any future routine author avoids it.

Adds one bullet to the architecture-principles list. No code, no behavior change — canon prose only.

{"number":350,"title":"google-identity: convert the three prose rules into skill-owned check-the-work rules","body":"Converts the `google-identity` pack's three prose rules (PR #-pending on this branch, commit 1b64b32) into deterministic checks, per the owner's direction: keep the pack, add a skill for the activity, move the rules into check-the-work tests, and delete all the prose.

## What changed

**The pack stays, prose-free.** `packs/google-identity/RULES.md` is deleted; `pack.mjs` drops `prose` and now mounts the new skill (`skills: ['google-id-token-validation']`), keeping the pack as the hand-declared anchor (`detect: null` unchanged).

**New skill `google-id-token-validation`** — a minimal SKILL.md (the trigger plus the three rule ids; no re-teaching, so nothing to drift) and a `checks.mjs` owning three rules, discovered by `skills/registry.mjs` and run at every Stop and in CI. The failure message is the instruction:

| Rule | Severity | Signature |
|---|---|---|
| `google-token-audience-pinned` | blocking | a config-format file (yaml/json/toml/tf) declaring the bare Google accounts issuer with no — or an explicitly empty — expected audience |
| `google-client-id-single-origin` | advisory | the same `…apps.googleusercontent.com` literal hardcoded in ≥2 files (a smell to judge: separate deploy units legitimately hold one copy each) |
| `google-token-email-verified` | blocking | handler code reading the `email` claim with no `email_verified` check, or strict-boolean-comparing `email_verified` behind an API Gateway authorizer (which stringifies claims) |

**Relevance gates** (a skill check runs on every repo): rule 1 scopes to config formats bearing the bare issuer origin — the path-form client OAuth URLs never match; rule 3 gates per-file on a verified-claims context and per-repo on a Google-identity marker, and skips test files; all three exclude the skill's own directory so its fixtures never flag the corpus repo. Code-form verifiers (jose/google-auth-library defaults) have no reliable file-scoped signature and are documented out of rule 1's scope.

**Answering "are you sure they weren't checkable?"** — the original commit was too conservative. There is no *universal* signature, but file-scoped signatures cover the grounded cases (the TLDR provenance is exactly rule 1's authorizer-config shape), so the rules convert; the signature-less residue (hand-rolled verifier code) is what the checks' comments document as out of scope.

## Tests

13 new fixture tests (scratch-repo harness), each rule proven both directions — violating fixtures find, clean ones (path-form OAuth URLs, per-deploy-unit copies, string-compared `email_verified`, marker-less repos, test files) stay quiet — and mutation-tested red (neutering `run()` fails exactly the violating-fixture tests). Full suite: 341 pass. Whole-repo sweep: clean (one new `file-placement` acceptance for the engine-lib import, mirroring the `unattended-agents` precedent).

Catalogs updated (`packs/README.md` row, `skills/README.md` entry) to satisfy `catalog-completeness`; the pack's `skills` list satisfies `skill-ownership`.

{"number":361,"title":"Local packs first-class: namespaced declarations; canon-curation moves to local_packs; local run_daily on by default","body":"Closes #360. Closes #364.

Two work packages on one branch. All decisions below are the owner's, recorded as standing decisions in `.claudinite/local_packs/claudinite/RULES.md`.

## 1. Namespace local-pack declarations as `local_packs/<name>` (#360)

Local packs were declared by bare id — the same namespace as canon packs, so a collision was only *caught* by `discoverPacks`' shadow guard, never prevented. The canonical declaration token is now **`local_packs/<name>`**, self-documenting in `.claudinite-checks.json`.

- **Engine, both forms accepted**: `packEntryId` strips the prefix (with `LOCAL_DECL_PREFIX` / `declTokenFor` exported); `loadConfig` normalizes at load, one layer below the runner, so unknown-pack validation *and* the interview/`packConfig` readers see bare ids whichever form the file used; the fleet's member-declaration read normalizes the same way.
- **Rollout**: a baselining declaration-normalization step rewrites members' bare local-pack declarations; the seed-style `local-pack-namespace` migration (`retire: 'auto'`) tracks convergence.

## 2. canon-curation → `.claudinite/local_packs/`; local run_daily ON; segregation via barriers only (#364)

- **`canon-curation` is now the canon home's local pack** (`.claudinite/local_packs/canon-curation/`, declared as `local_packs/canon-curation` — dogfooding package 1). The canon home's curation duties are Claudinite-maintaining-Claudinite: project-specific content on the home's own capture surface.
- **Local-pack `run_daily` scheduling is on by default**: `readLocalTasks` is `buildWorkPlan`'s *default* `localTasksFor` (still injectable; `localTasksFor: null` disables). A local task gates on the member's declaration exactly like a canon task; a descriptor worker path may be pack-relative or repo-root-relative (leading `/`). Every "experimental / not enabled by default / do not pass the seam" statement is purged (planner, local-tasks header, orchestrator routine, fleet DESIGN, packs/extending/skill docs). The moved canon-curation tasks are the path's nightly dogfood — an integration test plans the home's promote unit by serving the *real* descriptor files through a fake GitHub API, proving they are self-contained and worker paths rewrite correctly.
- **Packs-tree segregation is barriers configuration only.** The `pack-independence` code check is retired. The invariant is a barrier the moved pack *contributes* (`requires: ['barriers']` + `contributes`; the same composition `basics` uses for `claudinite-isolation`), keeping the same rule id so acceptances/overrides keep addressing it. Two new **generic barriers capabilities** carry it:
  - `siblings: "<folder>"` — each direct child directory guarded against the rest, expanded from the tree at scan time, fail-closed on an empty expansion;
  - `scope: "imports"` — relative import/require specifiers in code files only, matched across line breaks, resolved as module edges (extension/index completion, no bare/root-relative strings, no name/unique-filename layers, index-less directory import = breakage not crossing), so prose stays free to talk about packs.
- **Adversarially verified**: a workflow fanned out 4 stale-statement sweeps (all clean) plus a semantics reviewer diffing the old check against the new barrier; it surfaced 5 real divergences (untracked files invisible to the resolution index; comment/root-relative and unique-basename false positives; multi-line import false negative; bare-directory resolution divergence) — all fixed red-first, including building the barriers index from tracked **plus in-scope untracked** files. The barrier was also proven live by planting a real cross-pack import in the tree and watching the sweep go red.

## Verification

- All new behavior test-first (seen red before implementation): 65 barriers tests, local-tasks/planner default-seam tests, moved-pack contribution tests, migration probe, loadConfig/runner/registry namespace tests.
- Full suite green: **482 tests, 0 failures** (CI glob now includes `.claudinite/local_packs/*/*.test.mjs`); `node checks/run.mjs --all` clean; SessionStart surfaces (prose injection, skill mounts, interview, discovery) exercised end-to-end in the canon checkout.

{"number":396,"title":"scheduler: due-slot math + schedule config key (Phase 0 groundwork)","body":"Starts the vendored Actions scheduler for per-project maintenance scheduling (#394, DESIGN §2–3, MIGRATION Phase 0). This is the first, pure, well-tested slice of `engine/scheduler/`; **no behavior change** — nothing schedules or dispatches yet.

## What's here

- **`engine/scheduler/slots.mjs`** — the stateless due-slot math the scheduler runs each hour over the Actions run ledger (no watermark file). The whole model: consider only the *single most-recent* scheduled slot per frequency, and it's due iff its time falls in `(lastSuccess, now]`.
  - Misses self-heal to exactly one catch-up per frequency — never a backfill storm.
  - Hourly never backfills (its most-recent slot is always the current hour).
  - First run (no prior success) evaluates every frequency — the fresh-adoption smoke test.
  - Resolves the daily anchor ± offsets (anchor-dated slot ids, including the `daily-2h` hour-wrap when `dailyHour < 2`), the weekly weekday, and the monthly day-of-month with month-length clamping.
  - Pure: `now` and `lastSuccess` are always injected, so due-ness is deterministic and fully testable.

- **`schedule` config key** — added to `CONFIG_KEYS` with load-time range validation (`dailyHour` 0–23, `weeklyDay` Sun–Sat, `monthlyDay` 1–31). Absence is legal (defaults live in `slots.mjs`); its declaration is the per-repo cutover marker for the rollout.

## Tests

- `engine-tests/scheduler/slots.test.mjs` — slot math across the seven frequencies: miss→catch-up, double-run dedupe, first-run, hour-wrap, month-clamp, weekly rollback, hourly no-backfill, the full daily growth chain.
- `engine-tests/context.test.mjs` — `schedule` validation: valid / partial / absent, plus out-of-range and misshaped values.

Full suite green (508 tests) and the conformance sweep is clean for this change (0 blocking).

## Not in this PR (follow-on Phase 0 work)

`run.mjs`, `discover.mjs`, the signal collectors, `dispatch.mjs`, `validate-dispatch.mjs`, `verify-outcome.mjs`, `model-map.mjs`, `executor.md`, the workflow stub, the task-folder conversions, new checks, and the doc rewrites — each lands separately on top of this foundation.

A branch that **fixes the dedup routine** matches that too. Such a branch edits the canon and touches a local pack in the same change, which is exactly the shape of a corrupt prune — so the check reds the session on legitimate work.

const isDedupRun = work.commits.some((m) => DEDUP_RUN.test(m)) &&
